requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
I found no gaps; each obligation maps to code and tests, as follows.

**Implementation (`src/config.rs`)**
- `user_config_path_from` uses an absolute, nonempty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` on Unix and otherwise falls back to `$HOME/.config`. It appends `habeas/config.toml`.
- On Windows it uses `APPDATA`.
- `absolute_directory` rejects unset, empty and relative values, so `HOME` and `APPDATA` must be absolute and nonempty.
- `required_directory` fails with an `io::Error` that names the variable: "cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path".
- `ConfigPlatform::current` selects the platform, and `user_config_path` wires in the real environment.
- Usable across projects, and not project-relative or changed by project settings: `user_config_path` and `user_config_path_from` take no project root and read no project settings. `resolve_authoring` calls `user_config_path()` independently of `root`. These negative obligations hold by construction.
- Workspace settings use `habeas.toml`: this is handled by `workspace_location` (`load_workspace_config`, separate from the user path) and is only cited here.
- Other users of the path (`crates/habeas-sdk/src/redaction/mod.rs`) only cite the requirement to recognize the user file. They do not implement it.

**Tests (`tests/configuration.rs`)**
- `locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` covers an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, empty and relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to `HOME`, the Windows `APPDATA` path, and the error when no variables are set.
- `base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty` covers empty and relative `HOME` and `APPDATA` producing errors that contain the variable name. It also covers a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to an absolute `HOME`.

text: :::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
